results.summary: This design uses combinational logic gates (AND, NAND, OR, XOR, NOT) to control the segments of a 7-segment display based on eight switch inputs. It is intended as an educational demonstration of how logic gates can drive a display. The project is built in Wokwi and requires external switches and a 7-segment display for testing. The documentation is minimal, providing only a high-level description without detailed schematics or code.

This project implements a binary counter using flip-flops that increments on a clock signal and displays the count from zero to nine on a 7-segment display. It is designed for educational purposes, likely as a first design. Testing is done by manually stepping the clock to observe the count. External hardware includes a 7-segment display and a step button. The documentation is brief and lacks details on the exact circuit implementation.

This design is an 8x3 encoder that uses NOT, MUX, and AND gates to control LEDs based on switch inputs, with the goal of forming the letter 'A' when switches are set correctly. It is a simple educational project built in Wokwi. Testing involves toggling switches and observing the LED pattern. The documentation is sparse and does not provide a detailed schematic or truth table.

This is a logic puzzle where the user must set eight switches to light up the last LED, based on a hidden digital circuit. It is part of the Tiny Tapeout Puzzles series and is designed for educational entertainment. The project requires external switches and LEDs for interaction. The documentation describes the puzzle but does not reveal the circuit details, encouraging exploration.

This design uses an AND gate to control segments A, B, C, and D of a 7-segment display, with other inputs controlling the remaining segments. It is a simple educational project built in Wokwi. Testing involves toggling each input and observing which segments light up. External hardware includes a 7-segment display and switches. The documentation is minimal and lacks a detailed explanation of the logic.

This project controls a 7-segment display to show the letter 'H' based on switch inputs. It is a basic educational design built in Wokwi. Testing is done by turning on switches 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, and 8 to display the letter. External hardware includes a 7-segment display and switches. The documentation is very sparse and does not provide a schematic or detailed explanation.

This design outputs either a counter value or mirrors the bidirectional pins to the output pins, depending on a select signal. When sel is high, a counter is output on both the output and bidirectional pins; when sel is low, the bidirectional pins are mirrored to the output pins. It is a simple utility design built in Wokwi. No external hardware is required. The documentation is clear but brief.

This design implements an XOR gate with a registered output using a flip-flop. The flip-flop has active-high set and reset, with set unused. It is a basic digital logic building block built in Wokwi. Testing involves applying input combinations and observing the registered output according to the XOR truth table. External hardware includes a push button for reset, DIP switches, and an LED. The documentation is clear and includes a truth table.

This project is an encoder that uses NOT and AND gates to connect inputs to outputs. It is a simple educational design built in Wokwi. Testing involves flipping switches and observing which LEDs light up. No external hardware is required. The documentation is very sparse and does not provide a detailed schematic or truth table.

This design is a test circuit for a D flip-flop built from NAND logic, intended to demonstrate hold time violations. It is an educational experiment built in Wokwi. Testing is done by flipping switches and observing the outputs on LEDs. External hardware includes switches and six LEDs. The documentation is minimal and does not provide detailed timing analysis or schematics.
